solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cold suddenly affected pert young woman

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
to hit someone is to affect them suddenly, as news or an illness hits

explanation.surface: A cheeky girl is struck down by a sudden chill.
explanation.definitionFit: A chit is an old word for an impudent or forward girl, a slip of a thing.

clue.text: Almost set to tuck into chestnuts maybe with hot sauce?

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, as food is tucked into a mouth

parts.note: chestnuts are reddish-brown horses, an example of horses

indicators.note: the word for set loses its last letter

parts.note: a radio is a receiving set

explanation.surface: Eating roast chestnuts with a hot sauce, nearly ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chestnuts' tempts towards roast nuts, but chestnut-coloured horses are meant; 'set' is a wireless receiver.
explanation.definitionFit: Horseradish is a pungent condiment, often served as a creamy accompaniment to roast beef.

clue.text: Chap briefly shown round German plane

indicators.note: the shortened name goes around the abbreviation, enclosing it
the name is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: Timothy is a man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: A man gives a German a quick tour of an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tiger Moth is a classic de Havilland biplane, used for RAF pilot training.

clue.text: Saw what might be easily done

indicators.note: the clue asks what the two words could become, inviting a rearrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a job that looked like it would be no trouble at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the tool, but it is the past tense of see; 'what might be' turns EASILY DONE into a new arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means caught sight of or first beheld, a plain synonym of the past tense of see.

clue.text: Special formulation was our bond they say

indicators.note: the phrase is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: whatever was our bond linked us together

explanation.surface: A unique medical mixture was what held us together, people claim.
explanation.definitionFit: A linctus is a syrupy cough medicine, a specially made-up pharmaceutical preparation.

clue.text: One with rather evil bent cast as tyrant

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the letters are thrown into a new shape, as metal is cast

explanation.surface: An actor with a wicked streak is chosen to play a despot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent' looks like an anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; 'cast' rearranges I with RATHER EVIL BENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan IV of Russia, the first Tsar, was notorious for his cruelty and despotic rule.

clue.text: Woman beginning to encourage and tend soldiers

indicators.note: only the opening letter of encourage is wanted

parts.note: to tend is to incline or lean
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A woman cheers on troops and looks after them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tend' suggests caring, but means incline, as in lean towards.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleanor is a female given name, so a woman in crossword shorthand.

clue.text: American in boat that's cut fare from Japan

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits inside the shortened vessel
the vessel is docked its final letter

parts.note: a ship is a boat

explanation.surface: An American on a boat that has been holed, eating Japanese food.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish, so food from Japan.

clue.text: Going in starkers is good way to attract attention

indicators.note: the abbreviation enters the middle of the synonym

parts.note: starkers is British slang for naked

explanation.surface: Walking in naked is a fine way to get noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starkers' is British slang for stark naked.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudge, a gentle push with the elbow, is a discreet way to catch someone's notice.

clue.text: Business of bandits dressing to conceal equipment

indicators.note: the dressing hides the other piece by wrapping round it

parts.note: a bandage is a dressing for a wound
a rig is a set of equipment or apparatus

explanation.surface: Outlaws at work disguising their kit under wound dressings.
explanation.definitionFit: Brigandage is robbery and plunder, the trade practised by brigands or bandits.

clue.text: Employed engineers initially in Bucks?

indicators.note: the single letter goes inside the currency abbreviation, sitting in it

parts.note: bucks are US dollars, abbreviated USD

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word engineers is wanted

explanation.surface: Engineers given jobs in Buckinghamshire, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bucks' poses as the English county Buckinghamshire, but it means dollars, USD.
explanation.definitionFit: Something employed has been put to use, so the two past participles are synonyms.

clue.text: Coastal road announced for port

indicators.note: the phrase is spoken, giving the city's pronunciation

parts.note: a bay is a coastal inlet; a route is a road or way

explanation.surface: A seaside highway has been declared to lead to a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Beirut, capital of Lebanon, is a major Mediterranean seaport.

clue.text: Bag sent back — ecstasy widespread in island

indicators.note: the synonym for bag is turned round to read the other way

parts.note: to net is to bag or catch
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
rife means prevalent or widespread

explanation.surface: A holiday island where luggage is returned and party drugs are everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenerife is the largest of the Canary Islands, off north-west Africa.

clue.text: Protecting name, reveal chef sacked for unauthorised absence

indicators.note: the anagram wraps around the letter, guarding it
the letters are thrown about, as a sacked city is ransacked

explanation.surface: A fired cook, guarding a name, discloses the reason for being absent.
explanation.definitionFit: To take French leave is to slip away without permission, an idiom for absence without asking.

clue.text: Just one dropped round for gambling game

indicators.note: the numeral for one falls out of the synonym

parts.note: just means fair or equitable
I is the Roman numeral one
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A single person leaves, just as a round of a card game is played.
explanation.definitionFit: Faro is an old card game in which players bet on the order cards are dealt.

clue.text: Try to stop Southern Ocean bird

indicators.note: one piece plugs the gap between the others, as a stopper fills a hole

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south or southern
the ocean is a body of water
to hear a case is to try it in court

explanation.surface: An attempt to halt something in the Southern Ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Southern Ocean' reads as a place name, but it splits into S and a synonym for ocean; 'Try' is the judge's sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Shearwaters are seabirds that skim low over the waves of open ocean.

clue.text: Swimmer able to do the crawl?

definitions.text: Swimmer able to do the crawl?

parts.words: Swimmer able to do the crawl?
parts.note: not a stroke-perfect swimmer but a creature that both swims in water and crawls on land

explanation.walkthrough: 'the crawl' suggests the swimming stroke, but the creature literally crawls on dry ground too.
explanation.definitionFit: Frogs and newts live both in water and on land, swimming and also crawling about.

clue.text: Serving flyer has sorties to rearrange

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A pilot is told to reorganise their missions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flyer' suggests a pilot on sorties, but the definition is someone who serves passengers in flight.
explanation.definitionFit: A stewardess on an aircraft is a flyer who serves passengers drinks and meals.

clue.text: Region in small French islands excellent for climbing

parts.note: îles is French for islands

indicators.note: in a down light the letters go upwards, read from the bottom

parts.note: A1 is excellent, written AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: An area of small French islands that is great for mountaineering.
explanation.definitionFit: Silesia is a historical region of central Europe, now mostly in Poland.

clue.text: Scottish clan with the skills to produce great gumbo?

parts.note: gumbo is a thick Louisiana stew
art is skill or craft

explanation.surface: A Highland family famed for cooking fine Cajun food.
explanation.walkthrough: The gumbo is a stew, and the skill to make it is art: stew art.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stewarts, or Stuarts, are a Scottish clan, from which the royal house descended.

clue.text: Virtuoso on piano to establish tempo

indicators.note: in a down light one piece sits on the other; here the expert follows the musical letter

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft
an ace is an expert or virtuoso

explanation.surface: A star pianist sets the speed of the piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To pace something is to set its speed or rhythm, as a runner or conductor does.

clue.text: Dealer caught by dogged police officer?

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a dog handler is a police officer accompanied by a dog

explanation.surface: A trader is arrested by a relentless policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dogged' looks like persistent, but it means with a dog: a police dog handler.
explanation.definitionFit: A chandler is a dealer in supplies, originally candles, now often ship's provisions.

clue.text: Limerick perhaps shortened to make an impression

indicators.note: the word is cut by its final letter

parts.note: Limerick is an Irish county, an example of one

explanation.surface: A truncated comic verse still manages to be memorable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limerick' suggests the five-line verse, but here it is the Irish county.
explanation.definitionFit: To count is to matter or carry weight, which is to make an impression.

clue.text: Share Jill Masterson's fate? Cheerio!

indicators.note: to share her fate is to die inside gold paint, so the death word goes within the gold symbol

parts.note: in Goldfinger, Jill Masterson is painted gold, and AU is the chemical symbol for gold
her fate is to die

explanation.surface: A Bond fan wants to go the way of Goldfinger's gilded victim, then waves goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: Jill Masterson, the Bond girl in Goldfinger, is killed by being painted all over in gold: dying wrapped in Au.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is a French farewell used in English, much like the informal British goodbye.

clue.text: Wholesome? Worth buying? Credit refused!

indicators.note: the abbreviation for credit is turned away from the word

parts.note: credible means believable, worth buying in the sense of accepting a story
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: Questions about a healthy product's value, then a loan is declined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worth buying' suggests shopping, but it is the slang 'buy' meaning believe.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is edible is fit to eat, so wholesome in the sense of safe to consume.

clue.text: Military detachment to come together shortly

indicators.note: the synonym is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to unite is to come together

explanation.surface: A squad of soldiers will soon assemble.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a body of troops, a detachment forming part of a larger army.

clue.text: Mole finally quits a Baltic base, prepared for leave

indicators.note: the letters are made ready in a new form
the chosen letter leaves the word base
only the closing letter of Mole is wanted

explanation.surface: A spy leaves a Baltic base, ready to go on leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quits' takes E (the end of Mole) out of BASE, leaving BAS; 'prepared' then rearranges A BALTIC BAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabbatical is a period of paid leave granted, typically to academics, for study or travel.

clue.text: Handle we use to split explosive open?

indicators.note: the explosive is broken apart so the other pieces sit in its middle

parts.note: TNT is the explosive trinitrotoluene
a handle is slang for a name, and the one we use is our name

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a lever will crack open a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'open' is not the verb but a noun, as in a golf or tennis Open.
explanation.definitionFit: An Open is a sporting competition open to all comers, such as golf's British Open.

clue.text: Desire to handle dough is expressed

indicators.note: the word is spoken, giving a word with the same pronunciation

parts.note: to knead is to work dough with the hands

explanation.surface: A baker's wish to work bread dough is voiced.
explanation.definitionFit: A need is a want or desire, both nouns for something lacking and sought.
